correctness.rationale: Definitions and all quantifiers are explicit. The Euler-product series proves strict log-convexity of disk comparison function on all real x>2; disk containment and monotone convex chords reduce high k to a three-case strict barrier. The q derivative handles all k>=9. k=2,3 follow by exact finite-side stabilization. For k=6,8 a complete rational-interval certificate checks respectively 18 and 30 strict integer-power inequalities and proves infinite n stabilization. For k=4,5,7 exact A(k,5)+A(k,7)=2A(k,6) and strict concavity give every subunit exponent obstruction. Dowker convexity and AM-GM complete remaining exponents; source Theorem 1.3 transfers the valid log premise to tilings. Every numerical certificate has source and code in the same record; finite checking is only used for finite residual cases.

value.rationale: This is a complete sharp structural classification of the weakest exponent in the published polygonal honeycomb criterion. It strengthens a known average-perimeter conclusion to the qualitatively stronger geometric-mean/log-perimeter bound over all normal convex unit-area tilings for all nonexceptional regular even-polygonal norms. The three exceptional orders exhibit the exact discontinuity of the certificate threshold, and limitations prevent the negative certificate from being overread as a honeycomb counterexample.
